name: Facial hair as camouflage (weak chin)

lead: A beard adds apparent projection and definition along the chin and jaw, so a recessed chin or weak jawline looks stronger once it fills in.

Facial hair adds visual volume and an edge to the lower face. Wikipedia reports that in evolutionary psychology accounts beards signal dominance partly by increasing the perceived size of the jaw, and that clean-shaven faces have been rated less dominant than bearded ones. No trial has tested beards as chin camouflage specifically.

paras: People grow a beard for several weeks and shape the neckline and cheek lines, often keeping more length at the chin to add projection. Trimming and shaping matter as much as growth.
Low risk. Beards do not change the underlying bone, and patchy growth limits the result. Surgical options such as genioplasty are separate procedures with their own risks.

chain: Beard grown along jaw and chin
angle.text: Growing a beard along the jaw and chin adds apparent projection, making a recessed chin or weak jawline look stronger once it fills in. General research links beards to perceived jaw size and dominance, though chin-specific camouflage has not been tested.

lead: Facial hair as camouflage refers to growing a beard to mask a recessed chin or weak jawline. Proponents say beard shape and density add apparent projection and definition to the lower face.

Wikipedia reports that, in evolutionary psychology accounts, beards are said to signal dominance partly by increasing the perceived size of the jaw, and that clean-shaven faces have been rated less dominant than bearded ones, although the origin of beards through attraction versus male competition remains unresolved.[1] No published trial has tested beards specifically as a camouflage for a recessed chin.
infobox: Beard grown or shaped to alter perceived chin and jaw

paras: A recessed or "weak" chin describes a lower jaw that does not project far forward, so the chin appears to blend into the neck.[2] Beard styles that extend or squarely shape the lower face are used by some men to change that outline. The sources reviewed do not describe how beard styles interact with specific chin shapes.

Beards have shifted in and out of fashion. Reports note that Hadrian reportedly grew one to hide scars, that Peter the Great taxed beards in 1705, and that beards became fashionable again among young men in the 2010s alongside a large increase in male grooming product sales.[1]

Beards have been linked to masculinity, virility, wisdom and status, while in cultures where beards are uncommon they may be associated with poor hygiene or eccentricity.[1] Facial hair appears to influence rated male attractiveness, according to sources cited by Wikipedia.[1]

The chin is the forward-pointing part of the mandible, and a prominent chin distinguishes modern humans from Neanderthals.[2] Procedures described for correcting a recessed chin include genioplasty and, when jaws are insufficiently forward, orthognathic surgery.[2]
